text: Markdown linting plus structure-aware chunking for embeddings and graph search; preserve prior analysis that this is primarily a search/ingestion/schema feature with parser changes secondary, and deliberate whether Haiku plus a markdown linter should suggest or inject missing headings/subheadings to stabilize chunking and linking.

Feature intake: markdown linting plus structure-aware chunking for vector embeddings and graph search. Prior analysis: primarily a search/ingestion/schema feature and secondarily a parser feature. Preserve affected surfaces: src/services/parsing/markdown.rs and tests/integration/markdown_indexing_test.rs; src/services/ingestion.rs where markdown is currently ingested as full-file ContentRecords with MAX_EMBED_CHARS = 4096; src/models/content.rs and src/db/cozo_queries.rs because ContentRecord is keyed by file_path and lacks chunk metadata; src/tools/read.rs, src/services/search.rs, and src/db/cozo_queries.rs because query_memory and unified_search currently operate on whole-file records; src/tools/read.rs and src/db/cozo_queries.rs hybrid graph+semantic retrieval path for impact_analysis; reusable parser/metadata surfaces in src/services/parsing/frontmatter.rs and src/services/backlog_indexer.rs. Preserve design idea: a smaller or cheaper model like Haiku could work with a markdown linter to suggest or inject effective headings and subheadings into existing markdown so chunk boundaries become more stable and linkable. Preserve note: highest blast radius is the content-record model and retrieval pipeline, not only the markdown parser.

Spike: investigate markdown compaction / historical record condensation for token efficiency and retrieval quality in agent workflows. Assess where condensation is safe versus risky across historical docs, closure docs, memory docs, research notes, and, where appropriate, backlog artifacts. This is investigation only, not an implementation request. Preserve canonical source material while generating compacted derivatives rather than destructive rewriting. Evaluate compacted forms centered on decisions, plans, objectives, constraints, open questions, summaries, and key outcomes. Examine retrieval and token-efficiency tradeoffs, including whether compacted historical markdown could improve search, memory retrieval, and context loading. Consider whether smaller or cheaper models such as Claude Haiku 4.5 or GPT-5.4 Mini could perform or assist this condensation work. Related context: earlier stash item 180618FC on markdown linting / structure-aware chunking; keep this as a separate spike intake.

Add shell-visible indexing progress indicators to engram index and engram sync --full so long-running indexing clearly shows progress in the terminal; preserve the UX motivation that users may otherwise wonder whether the CLI is doing nothing; scope is specifically CLI/shell feedback during indexing workflows, likely touching CLI command UX, daemon or direct indexing progress reporting, and propagation of indexing progress to terminal output.

Add shell-visible indexing progress indicators for engram index and engram sync --full so users can see terminal/CLI progress during long-running indexing workflows instead of wondering whether the shell is idle or hung.
